title: The car came out spotless, but the smell was back the next week — why?

brief.idea:
Headline: The car came out spotless, but the smell was back the next week — why?

Subhead: Odour work is the only job a client can fail you on by smell — a week later, in a car that still looks flawless.

Reader: Studios taking on interior and odour work who have had a car come back, or who quote smoke removal by guesswork because they do not know how far it will go

Choose the 5 strongest of these beats — one per slide, keeping this order. The deck cannot hold all 9, so choose rather than cram:
- The job that comes back
- Why treating the air never works
- The headliner holds the most, and ruins the fastest
- Foam, carpet and the extraction that decides the result
- The cabin filter and the ducts
- Enzymes or fragrance?
- Ozone: read the machine's manual
- The cars to turn down
- This week

Close with a call to action asking the reader to DM the keyword ODOUR.

Do not invent statistics, numbers or percentages — use only facts stated above.

Lead with the reader's problem, not with the product.

BRAND VOICE: Quietly confident and aspirational, addressing the studio owner directly with understated elegance — evocative fragments over hype, with a flash of urgency when revenue is on the line.
PHOTOGRAPHY: this brand is carried by its images — most slides that show a place, a product, a person or a result should ask for one.
DO: Speak to 'you' and 'your studio'; Short, evocative fragments; Concrete business outcomes (bookings, rebookings, revenue); Let restraint imply premium
DON'T: Exclamation marks; Tech jargon; Overt hype or ALL-CAPS shouting; Generic SaaS clichés
SLIDES: exactly 7. Not one more, not one fewer — split or merge your points to land on that number.
WHAT THIS BRAND HAS TAUGHT YOU — these are corrections its owner made to your previous posts, more than once each. Follow them:
  · This brand's body copy is always cut after it is written — aim about 53 characters shorter than the budget allows.
  · This brand deletes the body rather than keep it — only write one when the slide is genuinely worse without it.
  · This brand reaches for the word "back" — use it where it fits.
  · This brand reaches for the word "liner" — use it where it fits.
  · This brand's headline copy is always cut after it is written — aim about 26 characters shorter than the budget allows.
  · This brand reaches for the word "substrate" — use it where it fits.
